data.narrative:
Nu Quantum, a Series A quantum computing company founded by Carmen Palacios-Berraquero, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 total peers: three public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and eight private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion. The company has raised $60M to date.

The stage-progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($60M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $120M. The peer-median method could not be applied: while six same-sector quantum computing peers exist in the dataset, zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-tier comparables met the minimum threshold of three datapoints. A sector-wide median would introduce unacceptable bias given the heterogeneity of valuations and business models across the quantum computing landscape.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M (low) to $138M (high), centered on $120M. This narrow output reflects reliance on a single method rather than true triangulation. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific cohort, the absence of verifiable peer comparables at identical stage and scale, and the nascent, capital-intensive nature of the sector which may render traditional stage-based progression metrics unreliable.
